overallNotes.personaArc: Tasha's arc spans ~3.5 years (Jan 2025 - Jun 2028) and follows a classic 'invisible laborer to recognized leader' trajectory. She starts as a 37-year-old bereavement coordinator at Transitions LifeCare, doing process cleanup beyond her title while managing stress (insomnia, jaw clenching, tension headaches). A near-cancellation of grief groups prompts her to build a structured pilot program. A family complaint about a missed referral handoff becomes a turning point — her own spreadsheet exposes the gap, and she shifts from patching holes to enforcing controls. Over time she expands from one protected workday into running a countywide bereavement program with six recurring groups, clinic referral partnerships, volunteer screening, a monthly dashboard, budget-approved admin support, and a modest raise. The work arc is paralleled by personal growth: repairing a friendship with Imani, deepening reciprocity with her aunt Denise, starting therapy for boundaries, discovering birding and cabin travel as restoration, and slowly considering adopting an older cat.
dataQualityIssues: ALL emotional_tone values are 'neutral' — clearly inaccurate for conversations with emotional content ranging from pride to grief to frustration. Many should be 'mixed' or 'positive'.
Summaries are often single quote fragments from the conversation rather than proper summaries (e.g., 'Blurry is the word', 'Better than I expected, honestly', 'Honestly, probably the checklist').

Tags are overly generic and repetitive (all slices include 'work', most include 'family', 'health', 'leisure', 'goals', 'housing') — they are regex-generated from high-level categories rather than describing actual slice content.
Decisions field in many slices is truncated (2025-03-05, 2025-03-29, 2025-04-22, 2025-06-11, 2025-07-02, etc.) — appears to be an 80-char cut like focus.

Slice 2025-01-21 has 'A lot has been shifting lately, and work finally tipped from vaguely messy into ' as focus — the sentence completion 'something I could not keep pretending would sort itself out' from Turn 1 would be more specific.
No slices carry 'negative' or 'positive' emotional_tone despite containing clear examples of frustration, relief, pride, and grief.
patternsNoticed: Recurring health-stress cycle: jaw clenching → insomnia → headaches → routine adjustment → improvement → recurrence under new stress. This cycles at least 4 times across the dataset (slices 2025-03-29, 2026-02-08, 2027-02-25, and references in others).

Tasha's signature coping mechanism: turning chaos into observable data (spreadsheets, legal pads, tracking logs, dashboards). She repeatedly mentions that seeing the pattern written down is what lets her act.
The 'beyond my title' refrain appears in nearly every work slice — Tasha is acutely aware of the gap between her responsibilities and formal recognition.

Denise Alston is the most consistent relationship anchor, appearing across time as emotional support, gentle nudge toward social connection, and eventually someone Tasha cares for in return (2027-06-06 marks a role reversal moment).
Imani the librarian friend has a specific care style (low-pressure nourishment, book swaps, no emotional excavation) that Tasha explicitly values and learns to protect.
Clinic outreach milestone (2027-04-14) is a turning point — external partners adopting the packet proves the program is real beyond Tasha's own organization.
Birding with Lena (2027-10-15) is the first genuine hobby Tasha picks up for pure enjoyment, signaling she has enough bandwidth for new interests.
There is a notable jump between slices — conversations cover ~3.5 years in 30 slices (about 1.2 months average between slices) but gaps range from 2 weeks to 3+ months.

relationshipNetwork.renee_holloway_lcsw_supervisor: Clinical supervisor who pushes Tasha on boundaries and body awareness. Intercepted Tasha's jaw-clenching in supervision, leading to tracking and dental guard.
